$comment: CORE VERIFIED SCHEMAS. Tracked in git on purpose: these were established against real exports, and a customer dropping a second export of the same shape must not have to re-earn them. User-LEARNED schemas are a different thing and are NOT here - they live in .session-archive/ (per-checkout, gitignored). See memory/decisions.md.

schemas.title: Pega / Splunk alert export

rejected.reason: named exactly like a category column and holds ONE distinct value across the entire export; ranking by it yields a single bucket containing every row, which reads as an answer and is not one

notes: elapsed_time states no unit anywhere in the export. The reading is sound; the UNIT is settled by owner ruling R10 as milliseconds, so it is reported as established and the report's columns say ms.

logger_name is the alias role (R13). It is stored here rather than left to name inference because the report labels a code with its logger, and a label printed off an unverified name is an unverified label. A logger serving MORE THAN ONE code is a coincidence and is deliberately not printed; the analysis refuses those on its own, from the data, and a config file cannot overrule that.
alert_code is the category role because alertType was measured against a real export and rejected below. Storing it keeps a second export of this shape from re-running the trap.
_time arrives as epoch seconds in some searches and ISO-8601 in others. Both are read.
There is no status column, so this export can say nothing about an error rate. The report must not print 0 percent.
